acrylic-rendering.q: How much does acrylic rendering cost in Australia?
acrylic-rendering.a: Acrylic rendering typically costs $30 to $80 per square metre installed, covering labour and materials. A 15-litre bucket of acrylic render runs close to $213, plus reinforcing mesh at $46 to $56 a roll for larger jobs. Final price depends on wall condition, the number of coats needed and whether old render must be stripped first.

acrylic-rendering.q: What is the difference between acrylic render and cement render?
acrylic-rendering.a: Acrylic render is a premixed, flexible coating with polymers added for crack resistance and colour consistency, while cement render is a sand-and-cement mix applied then painted separately. Acrylic dries faster and resists hairline cracking better on masonry veneer, though the premixed product itself costs more than a basic sand-and-cement mix.

acrylic-rendering.q: How long does acrylic render last?
acrylic-rendering.a: Acrylic render generally lasts 15 to 20 years before it needs recoating, longer than traditional cement render because its flexible polymer binder resists cracking. Lifespan depends on climate exposure, surface preparation and application quality. Regular washing and prompt repair of any cracks help acrylic render hold its finish and colour for the full period.

bathroom-tiling.q: How much does bathroom tiling cost in Australia?
bathroom-tiling.a: Bathroom tiling is usually quoted as part of a broader bathroom renovation, which runs $15,000 to $35,000 in Australia including tiles, waterproofing and fixtures. Porcelain floor tiles cost $28.90 to $125 per square metre and wall tiles $14 to $58.90 per square metre, plus adhesive and grout, before installation labour is added.

bathroom-tiling.q: Do you need to waterproof a bathroom before tiling?
bathroom-tiling.a: Yes. Wet areas like showers and floors need a waterproof membrane applied and cured before any tiles go down, because tiles and grout alone are not watertight. Skipping this step risks leaks into walls and subfloors down the track. A liquid membrane plus primer typically costs a few hundred dollars in materials for a small bathroom.

bathroom-tiling.q: Can you tile over existing bathroom tiles?
bathroom-tiling.a: Tiling over existing tiles is possible if the old tiles are sound, flat and well bonded, using a suitable primer and adhesive. It adds height to the floor and is not recommended in wet areas without fresh waterproofing underneath. Most tilers prefer removing old tiles first to check for hidden damage or mould.

colorbond-gutter-installation.q: How much does Colorbond guttering cost per metre in Australia?
colorbond-gutter-installation.a: Colorbond guttering typically costs $30 to $80 per metre installed in Australia, including labour and materials. A length of Colorbond quad gutter itself runs about $20 to $50 from suppliers, with Colorbond downpipes adding $7 to $37 per length. Final price depends on gutter profile, roof height and how much old guttering needs removing first.

colorbond-gutter-installation.q: Is Colorbond steel made in Australia?
colorbond-gutter-installation.a: Yes. Colorbond steel is manufactured in Australia by BlueScope at its Port Kembla plant in New South Wales, using a mix of local and imported steel. It has been produced locally since the 1960s and remains the standard prepainted steel used for Australian roofs, gutters, fencing and downpipes.

colorbond-gutter-installation.q: What is Colorbond gutter made of?
colorbond-gutter-installation.a: Colorbond gutter is roll-formed from zinc-and-aluminium-coated steel that is then given a baked-on colour coating for corrosion resistance and UV stability. This combination lets it handle harsh Australian weather without rusting or fading quickly, which is why it has largely replaced plain galvanised steel guttering on new homes.

deck-staining-and-painting.q: How much does it cost to stain and paint a deck in Australia?
deck-staining-and-painting.a: Deck staining and painting costs $40 to $70 per hour for a professional painter, with most standard-sized decks taking a day or two of labour once sanding and prep are included. A 10-litre tin of decking oil or stain costs $70 to $296 depending on the brand and finish, covering roughly 40 to 50 square metres per coat.

deck-staining-and-painting.q: How often should you restain a deck in Australia?
deck-staining-and-painting.a: Most Australian decks need restaining every one to two years, or sooner in coastal or high-sun areas where UV exposure fades and dries out the timber faster. Signs it is time include greying wood, peeling finish or water no longer beading on the surface. Regular recoating protects the timber and avoids costly sanding and repair later.

deck-staining-and-painting.q: Do you need to sand a deck before staining it?
deck-staining-and-painting.a: Yes, sanding removes the old, worn finish, greyed timber fibres and rough grain so the new stain can soak in evenly and bond properly. Skipping this step usually means patchy colour and a shorter-lasting finish. A light sand between coats on a well-maintained deck is often enough, while neglected decks need a full sand back.

fence-painting.q: How much does it cost to paint a fence in Australia?
fence-painting.a: Fence painting costs $40 to $70 per hour for a painter, with most standard timber fences taking a few hours to a full day depending on length and condition. A 10-litre tin of exterior acrylic paint costs $28.50 to $108.90 and typically covers 40 to 100 square metres per coat, so materials for an average fence run well under $200.

fence-painting.q: What paint is best for an outdoor timber fence?
fence-painting.a: Exterior acrylic paint is the standard choice for Australian timber fences because it flexes with the timber, resists UV fading and handles rain better than interior paint. A primer or undercoat is worth using on bare or weathered timber first. Oil-based options exist too, but acrylic is easier to maintain and recoat over time.

fence-painting.q: How often should a fence be repainted?
fence-painting.a: Most timber fences need repainting every three to five years, though fences facing full sun or coastal salt air can fade and crack sooner. Watch for peeling, chalking or bare patches as the cue to recoat rather than waiting a fixed number of years. Cleaning and priming worn sections first makes the new coat last longer.

gas-hot-water-system-repair.q: How much does gas hot water system repair cost in Australia?
gas-hot-water-system-repair.a: Gas hot water repairs are billed at $80 to $200 an hour for a licensed plumber, so a straightforward fix like a faulty thermocouple or pilot light often costs $150 to $400 in labour. If the unit itself needs replacing rather than repairing, a new gas instantaneous system costs $895 to $2,499 before installation.

gas-hot-water-system-repair.q: How long do gas hot water systems last?
gas-hot-water-system-repair.a: Gas hot water systems typically last 8 to 12 years for storage tanks and up to 15 to 20 years for continuous flow units with regular servicing. Age, water quality and how often the unit is used all affect lifespan. Once a storage tank starts leaking or rusting, repair is usually not worthwhile and replacement is the better option.

gas-hot-water-system-repair.q: Why does my gas hot water system keep going out?
gas-hot-water-system-repair.a: A gas hot water system that keeps cutting out is usually caused by a faulty thermocouple, blocked pilot light, gas supply issue or a failing thermostat. Dirty burners and poor ventilation can also trigger safety shutoffs. A licensed gas plumber needs to diagnose the exact cause, since gas appliances should not be opened up by homeowners.

hybrid-flooring-installation.q: How much does hybrid flooring installation cost in Australia?
hybrid-flooring-installation.a: Hybrid flooring installation costs $40 to $150 per square metre supplied and fitted in Australia. The flooring itself runs $31 to $99 per square metre depending on quality and thickness, with skirting boards adding a few dollars per linear metre. Final price depends on subfloor condition, room size and whether old flooring needs removing first.

hybrid-flooring-installation.q: What is hybrid flooring made of?
hybrid-flooring-installation.a: Hybrid flooring combines a rigid core, usually a mix of limestone composite and PVC, with a printed timber-look layer and a wear-resistant top coating. This construction makes it more water-resistant than laminate and more stable than vinyl planks, which is why it has become a popular choice for Australian kitchens, living areas and bathrooms.

Most hybrid flooring is highly water-resistant rather than fully waterproof, meaning spills and splashes are fine if wiped up reasonably quickly. Standing water left for extended periods can still seep into joints over time. It handles moisture far better than laminate or timber, which is why it suits bathrooms, laundries and kitchens so well.

leaking-shower-repair.q: How much does it cost to fix a leaking shower in Australia?
leaking-shower-repair.a: Fixing a leaking shower typically costs $30 to $80 per square metre for waterproofing and tiling work, billed through a licensed plumber or waterproofer at $80 to $200 an hour. A simple regrout and reseal with a leak repair kit and silicone can cost under $100 in materials, while a full waterproofing membrane replacement runs into the thousands.

leaking-shower-repair.q: What causes a shower to leak?
leaking-shower-repair.a: Shower leaks usually come from failed silicone seals, cracked or missing grout, a damaged waterproof membrane behind the tiles, or a faulty shower base or hob. Water finds its way through these gaps and can damage walls, floors and rooms below before it is noticed. Identifying the exact source usually needs a professional inspection rather than guesswork.

leaking-shower-repair.q: Can you repair a leaking shower without removing the tiles?
leaking-shower-repair.a: Minor leaks caused by failed silicone or grout can often be fixed by regrouting and resealing without removing tiles. But if the waterproof membrane underneath has failed, tiles usually need to come off so the membrane can be properly replaced. Patching over a membrane failure without removing tiles rarely stops the leak for good.

pool-paving.q: How much does pool paving cost in Australia?
pool-paving.a: Pool paving costs $50 to $150 per square metre installed for concrete or clay pavers in Australia. Natural stone runs higher: travertine pavers cost $109 to $359 per square metre supplied, so a stone pool surround commonly lands at $150 to $450 per square metre installed depending on groundwork.

pool-paving.q: What is the best paving for around a pool?
pool-paving.a: Travertine and other light-coloured natural stone pavers are popular around Australian pools because they stay cooler underfoot in summer than dark pavers or concrete. A non-slip or honed finish is important for safety on wet surfaces. Porcelain and textured concrete pavers are cheaper alternatives that still perform well if properly sealed and laid on a stable base.

pool-paving.q: Does pool paving need to be non-slip?
pool-paving.a: Yes, paving around a pool should have a slip-resistant surface since the area is constantly wet from swimmers and splashing. Honed, tumbled or textured finishes provide better grip than smooth, polished pavers. Most professional installers choose a slip rating suited to pool surrounds specifically, rather than general outdoor paving, to reduce the risk of falls.

roof-insulation-top-up.q: How much does roof insulation top-up cost in Australia?
roof-insulation-top-up.a: Topping up roof insulation costs $10 to $25 per square metre installed in Australia, depending on the current R-value and how much extra coverage is needed. A pack of R4.0 ceiling insulation batts costs $61 to $124 from Bunnings, so a DIY top-up on a small area can be far cheaper than a full professional insulation job.

roof-insulation-top-up.q: How do I know if my roof insulation needs topping up?
roof-insulation-top-up.a: Signs your roof insulation needs topping up include patchy or thin coverage visible from the manhole, rooms that feel hotter in summer or colder in winter than they should, and batts that are compressed, damp or gapped around downlights and edges. A quick inspection in the roof cavity usually shows whether existing insulation has settled or degraded.

roof-insulation-top-up.q: Can you add new insulation batts over old ones?
roof-insulation-top-up.a: Yes, adding a new layer of batts over existing insulation is a common way to boost the R-value without removing the old material, as long as it is still dry and in reasonable condition. Batts should be laid perpendicular to the layer below to cover gaps. Damaged, wet or compressed insulation should be replaced rather than covered over.

small-bathroom-renovation.q: How much does a small bathroom renovation cost in Australia?
small-bathroom-renovation.a: A small bathroom renovation typically costs $15,000 to $35,000 in Australia, covering the vanity, toilet, shower screen, waterproofing, tiling and an exhaust fan. Costs sit toward the lower end for cosmetic updates and higher when layout changes, new plumbing or structural work are involved. Trade quality, tile choice and fixture brand all shift the final figure.

small-bathroom-renovation.q: What is included in a small bathroom renovation?
small-bathroom-renovation.a: A typical small bathroom renovation includes a new vanity, toilet, shower screen, waterproofing membrane, wall and floor tiling, tapware and an exhaust fan. Many jobs also involve replacing plumbing rough-in and electrical wiring behind the walls. Because a small bathroom has less floor area, labour is often similar to a larger room even though material quantities are lower.

small-bathroom-renovation.q: Can a small bathroom be renovated without moving plumbing?
small-bathroom-renovation.a: Yes, keeping the toilet, shower and vanity in their existing positions is the cheapest way to renovate a small bathroom, since it avoids relocating drains and water lines. This like-for-like approach still allows for new tiles, fixtures and a fresh layout of finishes. Moving plumbing adds significant cost and is usually only worth it for a full layout change.

timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.q: How much does timber floor sanding and polishing cost in Australia?
timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.a: Timber floor sanding and polishing costs $40 to $150 per square metre in Australia, depending on the floor's condition and the number of coats applied. A 10-litre tin of polyurethane finish costs $60 to $318, with most floors needing two to three coats. Badly damaged or gappy floors sit near the top of that range due to extra prep work.

timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.q: How often should timber floors be sanded and polished?
timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.a: Timber floors generally need a full sand and polish every 7 to 10 years, though high-traffic homes or floors with a worn finish may need it sooner. A lighter recoat, without sanding back to bare timber, can often be done every few years to refresh the surface and extend the time between full sands.

timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.q: How long does it take for polished timber floors to dry?
timber-floor-sanding-and-polishing.a: Polyurethane floor finishes are typically dry to walk on in socks within 24 hours per coat, but need 7 to 10 days to fully cure before rugs, furniture or heavy foot traffic return. Water-based finishes dry faster than oil-based ones. Rushing this stage risks scuffing or marking the new finish before it has properly hardened.

water-damage-plaster-repair.q: How much does water damage plaster repair cost in Australia?
water-damage-plaster-repair.a: Water damage plaster repair costs $45 to $90 an hour for a plasterer in Australia, with small ceiling or wall patches often done in a few hours once the leak causing the damage is fixed. A sheet of plasterboard costs $28 to $97, plus jointing compound and tape, so materials for a typical patch run well under $150.

water-damage-plaster-repair.q: Can you repair water-damaged plaster without replacing the whole sheet?
water-damage-plaster-repair.a: Yes, small water-stained or soft patches can often be cut out and patched with a new piece of plasterboard, jointing compound and tape rather than replacing the entire sheet. Badly sagging, crumbling or mould-affected plaster usually needs a larger section removed. Fixing the source of the leak first is essential, or the repair will fail again.

water-damage-plaster-repair.q: How do you know if water-damaged plaster needs replacing?
water-damage-plaster-repair.a: Plaster usually needs replacing rather than just patching when it is soft, sagging, crumbling to the touch, or showing mould growth, since the paper facing and gypsum core have broken down. Discolouration alone without softness can sometimes be painted over once dry. A plasterer can press-test the area to check whether the board has genuinely lost integrity.
